quickAnswerTitle: Ohio School Calendars Are Set Locally
quickAnswer: Ohio does not publish one statewide K–12 attendance calendar. Local school boards adopt district schedules within state instructional-hour requirements. This collection currently includes Columbus City Schools, where even one district uses several calendars: Woodcrest Elementary starts in July, the traditional grades 1–12 calendar starts August 20, kindergarten starts August 25, and traditional Pre-K starts September 8, 2026.
about:
Ohio school calendars are adopted locally rather than issued as one statewide student schedule. State law requires local boards to hold a public hearing before adopting a calendar and sets minimum annual instructional hours by grade level. Districts still decide their own first days, breaks, professional-development days, conference closures, early dismissals, and last days.

The current Ohio collection includes Columbus City Schools. Its 2026–27 calendar hub contains a traditional calendar, a year-round calendar for Woodcrest Elementary, and separate Pre-K calendars for both schedules. Woodcrest grades 1–5 start July 23, 2026, while the traditional grades 1–12 calendar starts August 20. Kindergarten and Pre-K have later opening dates on each schedule. Columbus dates explain one reviewed district; they are not statewide Ohio dates.

Families should begin with the calendar assigned to the student, then check the school for bell times, transportation, testing, activities, emergency closures, and revisions. A districtwide calendar may not include every preschool, year-round, career-technical, online, or building-specific schedule.
calendarRulesDescription: Ohio sets instructional-hour and calendar-adoption requirements, while local boards publish the dates students actually attend.

calendarRules.label: No statewide student calendar
calendarRules.description: Ohio school boards adopt local calendars, so opening dates, breaks, staff days, early dismissals, and closing dates vary by district and sometimes by school or program.

calendarRules.label: Minimum hours depend on grade level
calendarRules.description: The state minimum is 455 hours for half-day kindergarten, 910 hours for full-day kindergarten through grade 6, and 1,001 hours for grades 7–12.

calendarRules.label: A public hearing precedes adoption
calendarRules.description: City, exempted-village, and local school district boards must hold a public hearing at least 30 days before adopting a calendar. The hearing addresses annual hours, school-day length, and the beginning and ending dates of instruction.

calendarRules.label: Ohio uses hours, not calamity-day allowances
calendarRules.description: Hours scheduled above the state minimum can absorb some lost time. If closures push a school below the minimum, the schedule must be extended or eligible online make-up hours may be used under an adopted plan.

calendarRules.label: Religious expression days are student-specific
calendarRules.description: Ohio law permits up to three excused religious expression days per student each school year when the notice requirements are met. These absences do not automatically create a districtwide closure.

stateSections.label: One Ohio District, Several Student Calendars
stateSections.content: Columbus City Schools shows why an Ohio family cannot safely use one generic first day. The student's school, grade, and program determine the correct opening and attendance calendar.

planningTips: Do not use a statewide holiday list as a student calendar. Ohio districts adopt local schedules, and a school or program may use dates that differ from the district's main calendar.
Confirm the calendar before saving a first day. In Columbus City Schools, Woodcrest, traditional grades 1–12, kindergarten, and Pre-K do not begin together.
Treat professional-development, records, conference, and early-dismissal labels according to the students named on the official calendar; they may not apply to every grade or program.
After a weather closure, check the district again. Ohio's hour-based rules mean a closure does not automatically map to a fixed statewide make-up date.
MySchoolDates ICS files are one-time imports and do not update automatically after a district or school revises its calendar.
commonHolidaysDescription: These labels appear on many Ohio district calendars, but the dates and attendance rules are local. Columbus uses the name Wellness Week for its full Thanksgiving-week closure and publishes separate year-round and Pre-K schedules.
verificationMethodology: Check current Ohio law and Ohio Department of Education and Workforce guidance for statewide calendar requirements.
Use the district's official calendar hub and current district-published files for actual student dates.
Keep traditional, year-round, kindergarten, and Pre-K opening dates separate when the district does not publish one shared first day.
Do not present Columbus City Schools dates as a statewide Ohio schedule.
Publish calendar downloads only after the visible dates and calendar scope have been checked against the cited district sources.

faqs.q: Does Ohio have one statewide school calendar?
faqs.a: No. Ohio school boards adopt local calendars within state requirements. First days, breaks, staff days, early dismissals, and last days can differ by district, school, or program.

faqs.q: How many instructional hours are required in Ohio schools?
faqs.a: Ohio requires at least 455 hours for half-day kindergarten, 910 hours for full-day kindergarten through grade 6, and 1,001 hours for grades 7–12. Different rules apply to community schools.

faqs.q: When does Columbus City Schools start in 2026?
faqs.a: The traditional CCS calendar starts grades 1–12 on August 20, kindergarten on August 25, and Pre-K on September 8, 2026. Woodcrest's year-round calendar starts grades 1–5 on July 23 and kindergarten and Pre-K on July 28.

faqs.q: Does every Columbus City Schools student use the traditional calendar?
faqs.a: No. Most students use the traditional calendar, Woodcrest Elementary follows a year-round calendar with intersessions, and CCS publishes separate Pre-K calendars for the traditional and Woodcrest schedules.

faqs.q: Does Ohio still use calamity days?
faqs.a: Ohio uses minimum instructional hours rather than a statewide allotment of calamity days. Excess scheduled hours may absorb some closures; otherwise a school may need to extend its schedule or use eligible online make-up hours under an adopted plan.

faqs.q: Can I add an Ohio school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Reviewed district pages provide ICS downloads that can be imported into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. These files are one-time imports and do not automatically sync later district changes.
